36-year-old male (68 kg) born and raised in rural Huehuetenango, Guatemala (family raised pigs; moved to US in 2021), with a history of aortic valve regurgitation on chronic warfarin 5 mg daily, presenting after a first generalized tonic-clonic seizure (2024-05-18), currently seizure-free on levetiracetam 500 mg BID (experiencing mild irritability).

1. Classification of Neurocysticercosis (NCC):
- Multiple parenchymal neurocysticercosis (>2 viable parenchymal cysts): MRI brain (2024-05-24) demonstrates 3 viable parenchymal (vesicular) cysts with visible scoleces in the right frontal, left parietal, and right occipital lobes (6-11 mm, thin nonenhancing walls, no edema) AND 1 degenerating (colloidal) cyst with ring enhancement and moderate perilesional edema in the left parietal lobe.
- No extraparenchymal CNS disease: No hydrocephalus, no intraventricular or subarachnoid cysts.
- Suspected ocular cysticercosis (extra-CNS): Per nursing telephone encounter (2024-05-28), the patient reports 2 weeks of blurry vision in the right eye with a mobile dark floating shadow.
